context_prompt:
Use the supplied email context plan across all its thread groups.
Reconcile earlier requests, the owner's responses and later acknowledgements in order.
Do not describe a multi-message thread as a single message. Supporting threads supply
facts only; they do not change the reply target, recipients or authorize actions.
Coverage is bounded: disclose omitted/truncated messages when material to the answer.
Attachment contents are unavailable. Prior assistant responses are not source evidence.
replay_command: THREADLY_REQUIRE_TEST_DB=1 THREADLY_TEST_DB=<isolated-postgresql-dsn> python -m pytest tests/test_mail_calendar_context_integration.py tests/test_shared_mail_context.py tests/test_calendar_creation.py tests/test_calendar_conversation_tools.py tests/test_assistant_migration.py -q
cases: Default provider thread versus explicit selected-message scope
Collapsed verification request, sent response and acknowledgment reach summary worker
Multi-thread reply and compose use all evidence with one exact reply target
Unread supporting reference rejected before workflow creation
Secondary source change rejected at hydration and before publication
Cross-owner plan rejected before provider access
Long recent mail cannot starve earlier evidence; sample keeps boundaries and reply target
Unchanged primary recapture keeps its version after a plan
Retained source handles survive searches and rehydrate on later turns
Historical single-message snapshots keep identical excerpts
Duplicate cards from one thread coalesce without expanding a selected subset
Reply generation, conversational editing and outgoing preview prefetch every source
Retained UI scope preserves its subset after pin changes
A new search preserves the already-read primary plan
Supporting evidence uses its latest read scope, including deliberate narrowing after a thread read
Retained mail handles coexist with pending Calendar details through Ask/Always clarification and idempotent action-status replay
limitations: No deployment or real email/Calendar writes
